candidates.context: Executive Summary • Scoping Study outlines an 8.0 Mtpa open-pit development pathway for the 100%- owned Jupiter Rare Earth Elements Project in Western Australia, producing a mixed rare earth carbonate (“MREC”). • Updated Mineral Resource of 1.7 Bt at 1,700 ppm TREO, including Jupiter’s first 160 Mt Indicated Mineral Resource, independently estimated by SRK Consulting at a 1,000 ppm TREO cut-off and announced on 12 October 2026. • Base Case economics demonstrate strong modelled outcomes, based on the Scoping Study Production Target and material assumptions set out in this announcement, including: o Pre-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.7 billion & IRR of approximately 56.0% o After-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.0 billion & IRR of approximately 48.4% o Estimated after-tax payback period of approximately 2.0 years from commencement of operations o Modelled life-of-mine sales revenue of approximately A$12.3 billion • Estimated pre-production capital of approximately A$556 million, supporting development of the proposed mining, beneficiation and hydrometallurgical processing operation. • Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources, with approximately 97% of the 107 Mt Production Target derived from Indicated Mineral Resources and 3% from Inferred Mineral Resources, based on a 1,500 ppm TREO plant- feed cut-off and following pit optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling. • The Production Target represents only approximately 6% of Jupiter’s total Mineral Resource, leaving approximately 94% outside the current mine plan and providing substantial potential for future Resource conversion, mine-life extension and/or expansion. • Conventional open-pit mining and integrated processing, with a favourable life-of- mine strip ratio of approximately 1.4:1, producing approximately 8,300 tpa of contained TREO in MREC (life-of-mine average) at a modelled overall TREO recovery of approximately 58%. • Exposure to all four principal magnet rare earths – neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium - which together represent approximately 23% of TREO, with yttrium also contained within and valued as part of the MREC basket. • Potential upside from iron, gallium and scandium, including potential iron concentrate production, which are excluded from the current Scoping Study economics and remain subject to further evaluation. • Broader Brothers opportunity - Jupiter is one of six rare earth discoveries across the 100%-owned Brothers Project and represents less than 3% of its landholding. 2

Sulphuric acid-bake testwork subsequently demonstrated approximately 90% rare earth extraction and was selected as the basis for the Scoping Study hydrometallurgical flowsheet.

Processing Flowsheet The Jupiter Scoping Study processing facilities are designed for a nominal 8.0 Mtpa plant feed rate and comprise two principal stages: beneficiation of run-of-mine material to produce a rare earth-enriched intermediate concentrate, followed by hydrometallurgical treatment to produce mixed rare earth carbonate (MREC). The proposed processing flowsheet comprises the following principal stages: Stage 1 – Beneficiation • Scrubbing and screening: Run-of-mine material is scrubbed to disperse clay and separate oversize material, which is ground and returned to the circuit. • Magnetic separation: Iron-bearing minerals are separated from the feed, producing magnetite- rich and hematite-rich streams and reducing the mass reporting to flotation. • Flotation: Rare earth-bearing phosphate minerals are recovered and upgraded to produce an intermediate rare earth concentrate, while rejecting the majority of the original feed mass. • Concentrate washing and dewatering: The intermediate concentrate is washed and dewatered in preparation for downstream hydrometallurgical treatment.

ASX Announcement

 20 October 2026 | ASX: CRI


Jupiter Scoping Study Defines Pathway to
Development
Critica Limited (ASX: CRI) (“Critica” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce the outcomes of the
Scoping Study for its 100%-owned Jupiter Rare Earth Elements Project (“Jupiter” or the “Project”) in
Western Australia. The Scoping Study is underpinned by the updated JORC 2012 compliant Mineral
Resource Estimate (“MRE”) announced by the Company on 12 October 2026, which established Jupiter’s
first Indicated Mineral Resource.

The Scoping Study was prepared by Sedgman Pty Ltd (“Sedgman”), with Snowden Optiro providing the
mine design and scheduling work and SRK Consulting (“SRK”) responsible for the Mineral Resource
Estimate underpinning the Study. The Scoping Study outlines a potential large-scale rare earths
development pathway based on conventional open-pit mining, beneficiation and downstream
hydrometallurgical processing to produce a mixed rare earth carbonate (“MREC”). The Study is based on
an 8.0 Mtpa processing design basis and evaluates the development of Jupiter’s near-surface rare earth
mineralisation, with the Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources.
Jupiter contains all four principal magnet rare earths: neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and
terbium. The Base Case attributes no value to iron, gallium or scandium, which remain subject to further
evaluation.

Executive Summary


    •   Scoping Study outlines an 8.0 Mtpa open-pit development pathway for the 100%-

      owned Jupiter Rare Earth Elements Project in Western Australia, producing a mixed rare

        earth carbonate (“MREC”).
    •  Updated Mineral Resource of 1.7 Bt at 1,700 ppm TREO, including Jupiter’s first 160

      Mt Indicated Mineral Resource, independently estimated by SRK Consulting at a 1,000
     ppm TREO cut-off and announced on 12 October 2026.
    •  Base Case economics demonstrate strong modelled outcomes, based on the Scoping

       Study Production Target and material assumptions set out in this announcement,
        including:

         o   Pre-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.7 billion & IRR of approximately 56.0%

         o   After-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.0 billion & IRR of approximately 48.4%
         o   Estimated after-tax payback period of approximately 2.0 years from

            commencement of operations
         o  Modelled life-of-mine sales revenue of approximately A$12.3 billion
    •   Estimated pre-production capital of approximately A$556 million, supporting

       development of the proposed mining, beneficiation and hydrometallurgical processing

        operation.
    •   Production Target overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral Resources, with

        approximately 97% of the 107 Mt Production Target derived from Indicated Mineral

       Resources and 3% from Inferred Mineral Resources, based on a 1,500 ppm TREO plant-

        feed cut-off and following pit optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling.
    •  The Production Target represents only approximately 6% of Jupiter’s total Mineral

       Resource, leaving approximately 94% outside the current mine plan and providing

        substantial potential for future Resource conversion, mine-life extension and/or
        expansion.

Development concept

The Scoping Study evaluates Jupiter as an integrated 8.0 Mtpa open-pit mining, beneficiation and
hydrometallurgical processing operation producing a mixed rare earth carbonate (“MREC”), with the
Scoping Study process design basis providing for approximately 9,300 tonnes per annum of contained
TREO in MREC at nominal processing capacity and the Base Case financial model assuming
approximately 8,300 tonnes per annum of contained TREO in MREC on a life-of-mine average basis.

The selected development concept is based on conventional open-pit mining using hydraulic excavators
and rigid haul trucks, with the shallow nature of the mineralisation supporting a relatively straightforward
mining configuration. Using a 1,500 ppm TREO plant-feed cut-off, the Scoping Study Production Target
comprises approximately 107.3 Mt of plant feed at approximately 1,879 ppm TREO, following pit
optimisation, conceptual mine design and scheduling, with an average waste-to-feed strip ratio of
approximately 1.4:1. This relatively modest strip ratio limits the volume of waste movement required per
tonne of plant feed, supporting efficient mining operations and potentially reducing mining costs,
equipment requirements and waste-rock handling relative to a higher-strip-ratio operation.

Processing is scheduled over approximately 14 years, including an initial processing ramp-up to the
nominal 8.0 Mtpa rate. The revised mine schedule is overwhelmingly underpinned by Indicated Mineral

and approximately 3.4% from Inferred Mineral Resources. Inferred Mineral Resources are distributed
across the mine schedule and do not comprise a significant proportion of plant feed during the early
years of the mine plan.

The processing strategy is based on beneficiation ahead of hydrometallurgical treatment, substantially

optimisation achieved approximately 14-fold TREO upgrading. Downstream testwork has demonstrated
production of MREC grading approximately 58% TREO.

Project History

The Brothers Project area was initially identified by Critica as having potential for clay-hosted rare earth
mineralisation through a review of publicly available geological and exploration data. The Jupiter target
was subsequently highlighted by coincident aeromagnetic and gravity anomalies together with
anomalous rare earth results from two co-funded WA DMPE Exploration Incentive Scheme drill holes.

Reconnaissance Air Core (“AC”) drilling at Jupiter was completed in June 2023, with every drill hole
reporting significant rare earth mineralisation within clay and saprolite zones. Discovery of the Jupiter
clay-hosted REE deposit was announced in November 2023.

Following discovery, Critica completed geophysical surveys and successive drilling campaigns to
delineate an approximately 42 km² area of clay-hosted rare earth mineralisation. Subsequent Resource
definition and infill drilling culminated in the updated Mineral Resource Estimate announced on 12
October 2026, including Jupiter’s first Indicated Mineral Resource of 160 Mt at 1,700 ppm TREO at a 1,000
ppm TREO lower cut-off.

Geological setting and mineralisation

The Jupiter deposit is located within the Murchison Domain of the Youanmi Terrane, Yilgarn Craton. The
Murchison Domain comprises greenstone belts, layered mafic-ultramafic intrusive complexes and
extensive granitoids emplaced between approximately 2.7 and 2.6 Ga. The Jupiter deposit is associated
with a previously unrecognised zoned alkaline intrusion developed within the regional granitoid terrain.

Jupiter is a clay-hosted rare earth element deposit developed through deep weathering of the underlying
alkaline intrusion. The intrusion ranges in composition from alkali gabbro through syenodiorite, syenite
and quartz monzonite and is concealed beneath transported cover. The resulting regolith-hosted rare
earth mineralisation extends across an area of approximately 42 km².

Rare earth mineralisation occurs principally within the clay-rich upper saprolite and lower saprolite zones
and forms a thick, laterally continuous mineralised horizon. Mineralogical studies indicate that the rare
earth mineralisation is hosted predominantly by florencite-gorceixite-goyazite and rhabdophane-
monazite, with lesser xenotime-churchite. Higher-grade REE mineralisation occurs as a broadly
continuous, sub-horizontal blanket near the clay-saprolite contact.

Exploration and drilling

Exploration at Jupiter has included geophysical surveys, Air Core (“AC”), Reverse Circulation (“RC”) and
diamond drilling, geological logging, geochemical analysis and mineralogical studies. A total of 770 drill
holes for approximately 45,937 metres were used in the updated Mineral Resource Estimate, comprising
exploration and Resource definition drilling completed across the Jupiter mineralised system.

Most of the Mineral Resource area is defined by drilling on a nominal 250 m x 250 m grid, which supports
classification as Inferred Mineral Resources. A central area of approximately 3.3 km² was subsequently
infilled to a nominal 125 m x 125 m drill spacing, including 145 AC holes for 7,274 metres, to increase
geological and grade confidence and support classification as Indicated Mineral Resources.

The drilling, geological logging, sampling, assay, density and mineralogical datasets were used to support
geological interpretation, Resource domaining and grade estimation. The observed continuity of the
mineralised zones and REE grades at the respective drill spacings supports the Indicated and Inferred
Mineral Resource classifications adopted in the updated Mineral Resource Estimate.

Metallurgy, Processing and Recoveries
The processing flowsheet evaluated in the Scoping Study has been developed from metallurgical
testwork undertaken on Jupiter mineralisation and is based on a beneficiation-first approach followed by
hydrometallurgical treatment to produce a mixed rare earth carbonate (“MREC”).

Jupiter mineralisation differs from conventional ionic adsorption clay deposits, with rare earths
predominantly associated with fine-grained phosphate minerals. The metallurgical development program
has therefore focused on physically upgrading the rare earth-bearing minerals prior to downstream
hydrometallurgical treatment, substantially reducing the mass requiring more intensive downstream
processing.

Stage 1 - Beneficiation Testwork

Jupiter’s clay-hosted mineralisation provides an opportunity to concentrate rare earth-bearing phosphate
minerals through conventional upfront beneficiation. The proposed processing pathway incorporates
attrition and screening, magnetic separation and flotation to produce an intermediate rare earth
concentrate. By rejecting a substantial proportion of the original feed mass before the acid-intensive
downstream processing stage, beneficiation reduces the volume of material requiring hydrometallurgical
treatment.

Beneficiation testwork has been undertaken across multiple laboratory and pilot-scale programmes,
including work at GAVAQ, Specialised Metallurgical Services, Independent Metallurgy and NAGROM. The
programmes have investigated magnetic separation, flotation reagents, mineral liberation and circuit
configuration to establish a suitable processing pathway for Jupiter mineralisation.

Initial bulk open-circuit flotation trials at GAVAQ demonstrated the potential to upgrade Jupiter
mineralisation across the four principal material types. As announced on 29 September 2025, these trials
achieved approximately 95% mass rejection and six-to-ten-fold TREO grade upgrading, producing
intermediate concentrates grading approximately 1.2 to 2.0% TREO.

Pilot-scale beneficiation testwork was subsequently conducted at GAVAQ using bulk composites
representative of Jupiter mineralisation. Optimisation of the beneficiation circuit achieved approximately
71% TREO recovery and 81% MagREO recovery, as announced on 14 April 2026.


                                                                                       32

Further optimisation produced an intermediate concentrate grading approximately 3% TREO,
representing an approximately 14-fold upgrade from feed while rejecting approximately 95% of the
original feed mass, as announced on 27 May 2026.

The Scoping Study has adopted a simplified beneficiation flowsheet comprising low-intensity magnetic
separation followed by flotation. Sedgman’s review of the testwork supports a single conditioning stage,
rougher flotation and subsequent cleaning stages as the basis for further development. Further testwork
will focus on mineral liberation, flotation reagent requirements and circuit configuration to optimise
intermediate concentrate grade and recovery and validate the flowsheet during subsequent study
phases.

Stage 2 - Hydrometallurgical Processing and MREC Production

Hydrometallurgical testwork has been undertaken at GAVAQ, Australian Minmet Metallurgical
Laboratories (“AMML”) and the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (“ANSTO”) to
evaluate leaching and acid-bake processing of Jupiter’s intermediate rare earth concentrate, impurity
removal and the production of MREC and mixed rare earth oxide (“MREO”).

Initial testwork demonstrated that atmospheric leaching using sulphuric or hydrochloric acid was
technically feasible, achieving rare earth extraction of up to approximately 60% under the conditions
tested. Sulphuric acid-bake testwork subsequently demonstrated approximately 90% rare earth
extraction and was selected as the basis for the Scoping Study hydrometallurgical flowsheet.

The proposed processing pathway comprises sulphuric acid baking of the beneficiated concentrate,
water leaching, staged impurity removal and precipitation to produce MREC. Initial ANSTO testwork used
approximately 1.4 to 1.6 tonnes of sulphuric acid per tonne of concentrate. Subsequent optimisation
programmes undertaken by ANSTO, GAVAQ and AMML demonstrated acid consumption as low as
approximately 1.0 tonne per tonne of concentrate under optimised conditions, representing a reduction
of approximately 30% from the initial testwork basis, as announced on 4 August 2026.

Impurity removal testwork at ANSTO demonstrated effective rejection of key impurities using a two-stage
neutralisation process. As announced on 16 February 2026, ANSTO successfully produced a commercial-
quality MREC grading approximately 58% TREO, with approximately 80% cumulative TREO recovery from
acid bake through to MREC precipitation. ANSTO also identified recycling of secondary impurity-removal
(“IR-2”) solids as a potential pathway to recover co-precipitated rare earths, with overall recovery through
to MREC expected to increase to approximately 89% in a commercial circuit. This potential improvement
remains subject to further integrated testwork and validation.

Further testwork at AMML subsequently produced a second MREC grading approximately 58% TREO, as
announced on 17 September 2026. This result closely replicated the product grade achieved by ANSTO,
demonstrating repeatable production of high-grade MREC across separate metallurgical programmes.
The AMML product contained approximately 15% MagREO, representing approximately 26% of its TREO
content.

For the Scoping Study financial evaluation, a combined downstream hydrometallurgical TREO recovery of
approximately 84% has been adopted. This assumption sits between the approximately 80% cumulative
recovery demonstrated by ANSTO from acid bake through to MREC precipitation and the approximately
89% recovery identified as potentially achievable through recycling of rare earth-bearing impurity-removal
residues. Further integrated testwork will be required to validate this recovery assumption and the
proposed residue-recycling configuration.

Jupiter has also demonstrated the production of high-purity MREO, including a representative product
sample grading 98% TREO, as announced on 23 September 2026. However, the Scoping Study has
adopted MREC as its Base-Case saleable product, reflecting the additional capital and operating costs
associated with producing MREO. MREO remains a potential alternative product pathway for future
evaluation.

Further hydrometallurgical testwork will focus on validating the optimised acid-bake conditions, refining
impurity removal and residue recycling, and confirming performance across the integrated downstream
circuit.

Processing Flowsheet

The Jupiter Scoping Study processing facilities are designed for a nominal 8.0 Mtpa plant feed rate and
comprise two principal stages: beneficiation of run-of-mine material to produce a rare earth-enriched
intermediate concentrate, followed by hydrometallurgical treatment to produce mixed rare earth
carbonate (MREC).

The proposed processing flowsheet comprises the following principal stages:

Stage 1 – Beneficiation

    •   Scrubbing and screening: Run-of-mine material is scrubbed to disperse clay and separate
        oversize material, which is ground and returned to the circuit.

    •   Magnetic separation: Iron-bearing minerals are separated from the feed, producing magnetite-
         rich and hematite-rich streams and reducing the mass reporting to flotation.

    •   Flotation: Rare earth-bearing phosphate minerals are recovered and upgraded to produce an
        intermediate rare earth concentrate, while rejecting the majority of the original feed mass.

    •   Concentrate washing and dewatering: The intermediate concentrate is washed and dewatered in
        preparation for downstream hydrometallurgical treatment.

Stage 2 – Hydrometallurgical Processing

    •   Sulphuric acid baking: The beneficiated concentrate is mixed with sulphuric acid and heated to
        convert the contained rare earth minerals into a form suitable for subsequent leaching.

    •   Water leaching: The baked material is leached with water to dissolve the rare earths into solution.

    •   Oxidation and staged impurity removal: The leach solution undergoes oxidation and staged
        neutralisation to remove impurities, including iron, aluminium and phosphorus, while retaining
        the rare earths in solution.

    •  MREC precipitation: The purified solution is treated to precipitate the contained rare earths as
      MREC, which is then separated and prepared as the final product assumed in the Scoping Study
       Base Case.

The Scoping Study acid-bake circuit is designed to operate at approximately 260°C, with a two-hour kiln
residence time and sulphuric acid consumption of approximately 1.0 tonne per tonne of dry
concentrate, reflecting the outcomes of the Company’s hydrometallurgical optimisation programme.

The Scoping Study has selected MREC as the final rare earth product assumed in the Base Case rather
than incorporating further processing to mixed rare earth oxide (MREO), avoiding the additional capital
and operating requirements associated with oxide production.

An additional feature of the proposed beneficiation circuit is the separation of magnetite-rich and
hematite-rich iron streams. These provide potential opportunities for future evaluation as additional
products; however, no revenue or value from iron has been included in the Scoping Study Base Case
economics.

Tailings and Water Management
Tailings Management

The Jupiter Scoping Study incorporates an integrated approach to tailings management, reflecting the
large proportion of plant feed rejected during beneficiation and the different characteristics of the
beneficiation and hydrometallurgical residue streams.

The processing flowsheet generates two principal residual streams: a high-volume beneficiation tailings
stream, produced through rejection of the majority of the plant feed ahead of hydrometallurgical
processing, and a substantially smaller hydrometallurgical residue stream generated from downstream
treatment.

The initial Scoping Study design provides for separate beneficiation and hydrometallurgical tailings
storage facilities, together with an effluent evaporation pond. The staged mine development sequence
also provides opportunities to progressively utilise mined-out pit areas for beneficiation tailings storage
as mining advances, potentially reducing the volume of tailings requiring long-term external surface
storage and the associated project footprint.

Further geotechnical, geochemical, hydrogeological and engineering investigations will be undertaken
during subsequent feasibility studies to confirm the suitability, timing and design of any proposed in-pit
tailings storage.

Water Management

The Scoping Study incorporates a high level of process-water recycling, with the objective of minimising
the Project's external raw-water requirement. Raw-water make-up is currently assumed to be supplied
from borefields, with raw water used to supplement process-water requirements and provide feed to the
reverse-osmosis (RO) water-treatment plant for higher-quality water required for concentrate washing
and hydrometallurgical processing. Further hydrogeological investigations will also evaluate the
groundwater resources beneath the Jupiter deposit and their potential to provide a sustainable water
supply for the Project.

Within the beneficiation circuit, water recovered from the tailings storage system is returned to the
process-water dam and recycled through the plant to the extent practicable. This recycling strategy is
particularly important given the scale of the proposed 8.0 Mtpa beneficiation operation and is intended to
reduce reliance on fresh make-up water.

The proposed hydrometallurgical circuit incorporates further water-recovery measures, including reuse of
RO brine for refinery-tailings repulping, recovery of purified water through RO treatment and recycling of
water from the leach counter-current decantation (CCD) circuit back to water leaching. Brine streams are
also proposed to be combined and reused where practicable to further reduce raw-water demand.

The current water balance represents a preliminary Scoping Study design basis and will be refined
through further thickening, filtration and concentrate-washing testwork. Additional hydrogeological
investigations will be required to confirm the location, capacity and sustainable yield of the proposed
borefield water supply, together with the integrated site water balance and water-storage requirements.

MREC Pricing

The Scoping Study Base Case assumes a gross MREC basket value of approximately US$52,800/t MREC
(US$52.80/kg MREC) and 75% payability against that gross basket value. The gross MREC basket value is
a modelled contained rare earth oxide value derived from the assumed individual rare earth oxide price
deck and modelled MREC composition and is not a quoted market price or contracted sales price for
MREC.

The rare earth pricing assumptions are based on Argus Rare Earths Analysis Data, May 2026, using its
Europe/US rare earth oxide price forecasts to 2040, expressed in real 2026 US dollars. These forecasts
have been applied to the rare earth oxides included in the Base Case MREC basket valuation.

Applying these price forecasts to the expected MREC composition produces a representative gross MREC
basket value of approximately US$52,800/t MREC. The Base Case composition is based on the MREC
produced by AMML and reported on 17 September 2026, grading approximately 57.9% TREO.

The gross basket value represents the contained rare earth oxide value of the MREC before application of
commercial payability and other product-sale deductions. The financial model applies an assumed 75%
payability to the gross contained rare earth oxide basket value, resulting in an assumed realised MREC
price of approximately US$39,600/t MREC, equivalent to approximately A$60,923/t MREC at the Base
Case AUD:USD exchange rate of 0.65.

Actual realised pricing and payability will depend on final product composition and specification,
customer qualification, applicable refining and commercial terms, and prevailing market conditions. No
binding offtake agreement or definitive commercial payability terms have been established at this stage.

Conclusion
The Scoping Study establishes a technical and economic basis for further evaluation of Jupiter as a
potential long-life Australian rare earths development. The Base Case generates a pre-tax NPV₈ of
approximately A$2.7 billion, an after-tax NPV₈ of approximately A$2.0 billion, a pre-tax IRR of
approximately 56.0% and an after-tax IRR of approximately 48.4%, with an estimated after-tax payback
period of approximately 2.0 years from commencement of operations, based on estimated pre-
production capital of approximately A$556 million.

Importantly, the production target of approximately 107.3 Mt represents approximately 6% of Jupiter's 1.7
Bt Mineral Resource, providing substantial Resource scale beyond that incorporated into the current
Scoping Study. The production target is approximately 96.6% Indicated and 3.4% Inferred Mineral
Resources.

The development concept combines shallow conventional open-pit mining with a beneficiation-first
processing strategy, substantially reducing the mass of material reporting to downstream
hydrometallurgical processing. Metallurgical testwork has demonstrated strong upgrading and mass
rejection through beneficiation and the production of high-grade rare earth products. The financial model
adopts an overall TREO recovery of approximately 58%, compared with the Scoping Study process design
basis of approximately 63%, providing scope for further recovery optimisation and validation during PFS.



                                                                                       48

Jupiter also benefits from its location in Western Australia's established Mid-West resources region, with
access to existing road and regional infrastructure and Geraldton identified as the preferred export
pathway. The Project provides exposure to the four principal magnet rare earths (neodymium,
praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium) within a broader rare earth product suite.

Critica has progressed Jupiter beyond laboratory process development into physical product generation
and commercial engagement. Representative MREO and potential iron concentrate samples have been
produced, and GAVAQ has now produced Critica's first representative MREC sample from Jupiter
mineralisation, with final analytical results pending. These physical products provide material to support
product evaluation, qualification and further commercial engagement. The Company is also engaged in
discussions with potential offtake and strategic counterparties. No revenue or value from iron is included
in the Scoping Study Base Case.

In addition to the rare earth products underpinning the Base Case, further technical and commercial
evaluation will assess potential additional value from iron, gallium and scandium, together with potential
alternative product and market pathways for yttrium beyond its inclusion in the Base Case MREC.

Overall, the Scoping Study establishes a development concept combining a large Resource base, a
relatively small initial production footprint, demonstrated beneficiation and downstream processing
pathways, strong Scoping Study-level economics, and exposure to magnet rare earths. Together with
Jupiter's Western Australian location, existing regional infrastructure and advancing product qualification
and commercial engagement, these outcomes provide the foundation for Critica to advance the Project
into a Pre-Feasibility Study.
